app.name: Market Day
app.demo: Demo mode — anything you save stays in your browser.
app.credits: Market data: USDA AMS, USDA FNS, USDA ERS, MassGIS / MDAR. Map © OpenStreetMap contributors.

status.noUpcoming: No dates in the next few months
status.unknownHelp: We couldn't read this market's schedule, so it isn't included in "open now". Here's what the source says:

home.title: Fresh food, close to home
home.lede: Find farmers markets open now near you, see what's in season, and learn where SNAP, HIP and WIC coupons are accepted.
home.locationError: We couldn't get your location. Try typing an address instead.
home.addressNotFound: We couldn't find that address. Try a street and town.
home.seeMap: See all markets on the map
home.benefitsBody: At HIP markets, every SNAP dollar you spend on fruits and vegetables comes back on your card, up to a monthly limit.
home.staleNote: Schedules come from public listings that may be out of date: Massachusetts from the state's 2023 list, everywhere else from USDA's 2014 national directory. Check with the market before you go.

explore.title: Markets map
explore.needLocation: Set your location on the home page to filter by distance.
explore.lilaLegend: Shaded: census tracts the USDA lists as low income and low access to food stores (1 mile urban / 10 miles rural).
explore.mapLabel: Map of markets. The list shows the same markets and works with a keyboard and screen reader.
explore.zoomForTracts: Zoom in to see low-income / low-access areas

filters.sustainable: Has a vendor scoring 60+ on sustainability
filters.sampleNote: Products and payment methods are from sample vendor data.

market.stale: This listing hasn't been updated in over a year. Check with the market before you go.
market.checkinBody: At the market, scan this code (or tap the button) to earn points. One check-in per market per day.
market.tract: This market is in a census tract the USDA lists as {{what}}.
market.both: low income and low access to food stores
market.biweekly: Every-other-week dates are estimated. Confirm with the market.
market.timeZone: Times are local to the market ({{zone}}).

search.inSeason: {{crop}} are in season in the {{region}} now.
search.outOfSeason: In the {{region}}, {{crop}} are usually in season in {{months}}. Markets may still have stored or greenhouse crops.

seasonal.title: What's in season
seasonal.lede: Locally grown crops by month for your region. Tap a crop to find markets that sell it.
seasonal.source: Approximate months compiled from USDA SNAP-Ed and state seasonal guides (Northeast from MassGrown). Weather and elevation shift things by a few weeks.
seasonal.none: Not much is harvested this month — storage crops and greenhouse greens carry the markets.

benefits.title: Using SNAP, HIP and WIC at farmers markets
benefits.lede: Many Massachusetts markets accept food benefits, and some give you extra money for fruits and vegetables.
benefits.spendLabel: How much SNAP will you spend on fruits and vegetables?
benefits.result: You'd get {{refund}} back on your card.
benefits.example: Example: spend {{spend}} of SNAP on eligible produce at a HIP vendor → get {{back}} back on your card.
benefits.remember: Remember my household size on this device
benefits.rememberHelp: Off by default. We never send this anywhere.
benefits.noAmounts: Program amounts change. Always check the official page.

rewards.title: My market rewards
rewards.lede: Earn points each time you check in at a market. Points are for fun in this demo.
rewards.methodBody: We assume a typical visit is about {{dollars}} and {{lbs}} lb of food. Conventional produce travels about {{conv}} miles (Leopold Center estimate); we compare that with the sample vendors' farm distances and use EPA's truck emission factor of {{factor}} kg CO₂e per ton-mile. These are rough estimates.
rewards.empty: No check-ins yet. Look for the QR code at the market info table, or on any market page.

checkin.title: Market check-in
checkin.already: You've already checked in here today. Come back next market day.
checkin.badToken: This check-in code isn't valid today. Scan the code at the market.

portal.title: Vendor portal
portal.lede: Update what you're selling, your prices and where you'll be. Pick a sample vendor to try it.
portal.saved: Saved. Shoppers on this device see your changes.
portal.assessmentHelp: Your score updates as you check boxes. Self-reported items stay marked until verified.
portal.surplusHelp: List what's left at the end of the day. Shoppers see it on the market page.

manager.title: Market manager
manager.lede: Edit a sample market's schedule, post closures, and review vendor applications.

scores.title: How sustainability scores work
scores.lede: Each vendor's score is out of 100, from six categories. The formula is public so vendors know how to improve. Items marked self-reported haven't been verified yet.

about.title: About the data
about.lede: Market Day is a static website. Public data is collected weekly by a build script, checked, and published as files — nothing about you is sent to a server.
about.sampleBody: Market locations, schedules and food-benefit participation are real public data from Massachusetts and USDA. Vendors, products, prices and anything you save are sample data for the demo, and are labelled "Sample data".
